overturn_protocol.metric: The count of failed lifecycle cases (ambiguous submit, duplicate/restart, partial/cancel, stale/clock/risk, request budget, ownership, kill) on identical fixtures. Also, for any broker run: whether the reconciliation matched (positions, open orders, cash delta) and how many additional writes recovery made.

overturn_when: The verdict changes if either of two checks has a different outcome. First, an open-session run of the c5 Nautilus-integrated path (blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper runner.py paper, then recover) produces a receipt with a reconciliation mismatch, a duplicate write or an unresolved order. Second, an executed same-fixture comparison shows fewer failures for c2's order gate or a c3 strict schema than the current adapter. That comparison runs the lifecycle tests in tests/test_adaptive_paper_safety.py, tests/test_adaptive_paper_recovery.py and tests/test_adaptive_paper_native.py with python3 -m unittest. For IBKR, a native Nautilus IBKR paper receipt that passes ownership, reconciliation and partial/cancel/reconnect cases would promote c7.

It also documents a durable SQLite journal and ambiguous submissions that are never blindly retried. The suite results are documented, not re-run here: 893 of 895 passed with 2 skipped, and 42 unchanged upstream Nautilus adapter-template tests passed. Its native_capacity run is synthetic: 180 submissions, 90 roundtrips, broker_connections 0 and paper_orders 0.
